events.label: Battle of Isly
events.summary: Moroccan army under the sultan's son Sidi Mohammed destroyed by Bugeaud's French force; led to the Treaty of Tangier and the Lalla Maghnia border convention.
events.mainDispute: Moroccan troop numbers and casualties, which French accounts inflate. Whether the defeat was as total as French reporting claimed.

events.label: Hispano-Moroccan War and the Treaty of Wad Ras
events.summary: Spanish invasion and capture of Tetouan; the resulting indemnity mortgaged Moroccan customs revenue for decades.
events.mainDispute: The real burden of the indemnity as a share of state revenue. Whether Britain brokered the terms to protect its own commercial position.

events.label: Madrid Conference on protection
events.summary: Convened at Hassan I's request to limit consular protection; instead codified it and granted foreigners the right to own land in Morocco.
events.mainDispute: How many protected persons there actually were, and what share of taxable wealth they removed from the Makhzen.

events.label: Act of Algeciras
events.summary: International conference following the First Moroccan Crisis; established the State Bank of Morocco and European supervision of customs and police while formally affirming Moroccan sovereignty.
events.mainDispute: Whether it was a genuine multilateral guarantee or a managed transfer of Morocco to France with German consent purchased later.

events.label: Casablanca 1907 — killings, bombardment and occupation
events.summary: Killing of nine European port workers on 30 July 1907 followed by French naval bombardment 5-7 August, landing, sack of the city, and the occupation of the Chaouia — the first permanent French military presence in Atlantic Morocco.
events.mainDispute: The death toll, where estimates range from 600 to well over 3,000. Whether the bombardment was a proportionate protection of nationals or a pre-planned seizure. Responsibility for the looting.

events.label: Treaty of Fez and the April 1912 rising
events.summary: Treaty of 30 March 1912 establishing the French protectorate, signed by Abdelhafid and Regnault; the Fez rising of 17 April 1912 on its disclosure; and the Franco-Spanish treaty of 27 November 1912 partitioning the country.
events.mainDispute: Whether the Arabic and French texts differ in substance — the foundation of the Moroccan legal argument that the protectorate was void. Casualties in the April rising. Whether the rising was a soldiers' mutiny over pay or a political insurrection.

events.label: Battle of El Herri
events.summary: A French column of 1,230 men under Lt-Col Laverdure raided Mouha ou Hammou Zayani's camp without orders, then was destroyed during its withdrawal. 623 French and colonial troops killed — France's heaviest single defeat in Morocco.
events.mainDispute: Zaian casualties (the French battlefield count of 182 is a French count). Whether responsibility lies with Laverdure's indiscipline (the official French line) or with Lyautey's wartime force posture. Whether the raid's aim was Hammou himself or his camp.

events.label: Annual and the Rif War
events.summary: Spanish military collapse in the eastern Rif in July-August 1921, followed by five years of war against the Rif Republic ending with Abd el-Krim's surrender to France at Targuist, 26 May 1926.
events.mainDispute: Total Spanish dead (7,875 to 13,363). Silvestre's manner of death. Alfonso XIII's alleged encouragement of the advance. Whether Monte Arruit was a massacre after surrender on terms or a fight that continued. The scale of Spanish chemical weapons use.

events.label: The Berber Dahir
events.summary: Dahir of 16 May 1930 placing Tamazight-speaking tribes under customary-law tribunals with serious crime before French courts; triggered the Ya Latif campaign and the emergence of mass Moroccan nationalism.
events.mainDispute: Whether it was a deliberate de-Islamisation plot or an extension of existing legislation that was received as one. Whether Mohammed V signed freely.

events.label: Deposition, exile and return of Mohammed V
events.summary: The French Residency and a coalition of pashas and qaids led by El Glaoui deposed the sultan and installed Ben Arafa; two years of resistance forced his return and led directly to independence.
events.mainDispute: Who decided — Paris, the Residency, or El Glaoui. Casualty figures in the resistance of 1953-55. Whether the Army of Liberation or the negotiations produced independence.

uncertain.label: Ma al-ʿAynayn appointed khalifa of the Sahara
uncertain.subject: ma-al-aynayn
uncertain.why: A dahir appointing him representative over Saharan territories. The date determines whether the act preceded or responded to Spanish occupation at Dakhla — which is the crux of the modern territorial argument.

uncertain.label: Mouha ou Hammou Zayani invested as qaid of the Zaian
uncertain.subject: mouha-ou-hammou-zayani
uncertain.why: Three different years — 1877, 1880 and 1886 — appear in works of comparable authority.

uncertain.label: Mouha ou Hammou Zayani born
uncertain.subject: mouha-ou-hammou-zayani
uncertain.why: c. 1857 or c. 1863, Middle Atlas — not established.
